scope: Incremental public-source priority/applicability audit only. No correctness verdict, computation, file mutation, model calls, or external contact. The v3 parent note and scout were read first; their checked Zhu/Margolis–Schnabel/Menon work is reused.

summary.local_mechanisms: The index-3 subgroup construction is an elementary stabilizer/product-set argument with close published antecedents. Once the required subgroup products and cross-coset incidence are supplied, intersection index 9 and the cell bijection are routine consequences of published identities. The contradiction inside a cell is an exact Sun(3) application.
summary.whole_candidates: No primary statement located in this incremental screen directly excludes the CASEA/CELL patterns or the complete distinct-2/3-marker family under the candidate's exact hypotheses. This is a bounded no-hit, not novelty.
summary.calibration: Routine/corollary at the local-lemma level; a potential modest specialist extension at the complete tuple-family level, conditional on every pending classification and transfer premise. A consequential result is not established.

target_hypotheses.F: Seven indices n_i=6r_i, with pairwise coprime positive r_i. There are distinct vertices z,t with 2|r_z and 3|r_t. Exponents are unbounded; a possible factor 5 occurs in at most one r_i.
target_hypotheses.a1: r_z=2^E 5^Bz w_z, r_t=3^A 5^Bt w_t, E,A>=1, Bz*Bt=0; the other five vertices are unmarked.
target_hypotheses.a2: A distinct p has r_p=5^B w_p, B>=1; r_z=2^E w_z, r_t=3^A w_t; the four remaining vertices are unmarked.
target_hypotheses.status: The map's branch exclusions remain conditional. Its exhaustion argument is not an emptiness proof. The addendum adds material prerequisites rather than certifying the earlier chain.

new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.source: Sambale, On the complement of a union of cosets, Theorems 1–3
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.read_scope: Theorems 1–3 and Lemma 5; the equality proof was also read. Earlier scouting had only title/abstract coverage.
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.quote: Then there exist t₁,...,t_m∈G with G=t₁A∪...∪t_mA and m≤2ⁿ.
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.checked_statement: For n individual subgroup cosets with nonempty complement A, |A|>=|G|/2^n in finite G. Theorem 2 characterizes equality by A=aK, K=intersection H_i, [G:K]=2^n. Theorem 3 requires an irredundant cover.
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.relevance: A later, genuinely overlapping complement/equality theorem, but not a matched implication of CELL or F.

new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.read_scope: Introduction: exact partition definition and both main theorem statements; not a new full-paper audit
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.quote: The Herzog-Schönheim Conjecture is true for symmetric groups.
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.checked_statement: Theorem 1.3 gives the corresponding result for simple groups.
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.relevance: Requires a partition of the whole group and concludes repeated indices. It does not assert Sun(7) for disjoint, non-covering families.

new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.read_scope: Introduction and main theorem statements, pp. 1–6; proofs not audited
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.quote: If there exists a d_s-cycle in T_s, then the index d_s appears in the partition at least p times
new_verified_primary_evidence_beyond_v3.relevance: Again a complete coset partition, with an additional transition-group cycle condition. The finitely generated-group transfer in Theorem 6 retains these partition hypotheses.

exact_hypothesis_comparisons.candidate_premises: At normalized apex a: D_j=D_k, mu(D_j)+mu(U_aU_j)=1, x_aj=x_jk=2.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.matched: Finite product-set cardinality, invariance, generated-subgroup containment, and equal-cardinality coincidence are classical mechanisms. MS37/MS46 explicitly use closely related product equalities to obtain subgroups.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.unmatched: MS37 is not a direct substitution: with a=6 the candidate has multipliers 2 rather than the required 1; with a=3 its cofactors are 2r_i and are not pairwise coprime. MS46's surrounding five-term hypotheses also do not match.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.important_scope: SUB does not automatically identify U_aU_k with K: the candidate itself requires x_ak=2 for that additional equality/distinct-coset conclusion.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.assessment: [INFERENCE: applicability comparison] Routine elementary consequence conditional on the asserted complement equality, not a direct invocation of MS37 and not an independently established new subgroup theorem.

exact_hypothesis_comparisons.candidate: CELL Lemma CELL(i): [G:K intersection L]=9 and nine cells
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.candidate_premises: [G:K]=[G:L]=3; an L-vertex U_x is contained in L and meets all three K-cosets, so U_xK=G; corresponding K/L vertex-incidence hypotheses supply pieces in every cell.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.matched: Margolis–Schnabel Lemma 3.2(2), already checked in v3, gives the product-cardinality identity. Together with LK=G it gives index 9. Z32 then gives the bijection between the nine coset pairs and intersection cosets.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.unmatched: K!=L alone is not the premise used for index 9. The cross-coset transitivity/product-equals-G input is essential. The prescribed pieces and their indices require the additional U_v containment and m=3 data.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.important_scope: This is a bijection of coset sets. No normality is required, and no quotient-group identification with C3×C3 follows merely from it.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.assessment: [INFERENCE: applicability comparison] Routine/corollary once those incidence hypotheses are supplied; the literature identities do not supply them from the original seven indices.

exact_hypothesis_comparisons.primary: Zhu Theorem 1.1 / Theorem 2.2; Margolis–Schnabel Proposition 4.2, reused from v3
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.candidate_premises: Translate a nonempty cell to H=K intersection L. The three pieces must be nonempty, pairwise disjoint left cosets of subgroups of H, with finite indices whose pairwise gcds are all <=2.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.matched: Exactly the k=3 hypothesis/conclusion of Zhu: three disjoint finite-index cosets require a pair of index gcd at least 3. For the displayed even indices with pairwise coprime cofactors, MS Proposition 4.2 is the same instance.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.unmatched: Sun(3) does not establish that all required pieces exist, that their indices are n_v/3, or that the z-piece has the asserted prime support. Those are antecedent obligations in CELL.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.a2_comparison: A p-piece has index 2*5^B*w_p, rather than 2*w_p. This remains compatible with the claimed cell-level gcd test only because the other actual cofactors carry no 5. It does not license treating every auxiliary A2 label as coprime.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.assessment: Exact classical contradiction, conditional on the candidate's piece/index data; no correctness acceptance of those data.

exact_hypothesis_comparisons.matched: EQ uses saturation of capacity inequalities; IN localizes the classical fibre count of Zhu Lemma 3.3 and removes the apex's occupied fibre. The v3 M-S Lemma 3.5 equality/counting precedent remains relevant.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.unmatched: The specific 5/6 upper bound, equality-for-every-occupied-fibre clause, cross-apex transfers, and exhaustive five-vertex classification are not supplied by the quoted public lemmas.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.casea_scope: K23 classifies Case A only after excluding the all-(2,2) type and importing the stated row/transfer claims. It is not itself an exclusion of the K2,3 survivor.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.assessment: [INFERENCE: calibration] Elementary assemblies, but no exact published statement matching the complete classification was located. It would be inaccurate either to label the entire package an immediate published theorem or to advertise its elementary substeps as a new method.

exact_hypothesis_comparisons.candidate: Full distinct-marker family F versus prior family theorems
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.reused_primary: Menon Theorem 4.2, arXiv:2608.15873v1, and M-S Proposition 4.7 / Lemma 4.6, as checked in the prior scouts.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.matched: Arbitrary groups and disjoint finite-index cosets.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.unmatched: Menon's family requires two indices 3r_1,3r_2 with r_1,r_2 odd. Every F index is divisible by 6, so those two required entries are absent. M-S Proposition 4.7 additionally requires an index exactly 3. Deleting cosets and invoking Sun(k) for k<=6 gives no gcd contradiction: the original pairwise gcd 6 already satisfies those lower bounds.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.assessment: No direct whole-family corollary of these checked tuple theorems. That does not prove absence of another equivalent result.

exact_hypothesis_comparisons.SAMB: Its complement bound can apply to individual cosets when their union is proper, but it has no seven-index gcd conclusion. The candidate D_j are generally double cosets/unions of cosets, not one subgroup coset each. Neither a controlled n-coset representation nor the required dyadic equality is supplied for importing its equality classification.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.GM_CH: Their complete-partition hypotheses and, respectively, ambient-group or cycle hypotheses are not the F hypotheses. The derived three K-cosets already have repeated index 3, so an HSC multiplicity conclusion is not a contradiction.
exact_hypothesis_comparisons.assessment: Newly checked statement-level counterevidence against conflating nearby cover/partition results with a Sun(7) or CELL theorem.
